subject: Remediation verification digest request — Widgetly pen test (SOC 2 scope)
messages:
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@widgetly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: securityops@widgetly.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-remediation validation request — Widgetly pen test (SOC2)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for working with us on the recent penetration test. Our security team has completed the remediation work against the findings in the RedTeam report (reference attached: widgetly_remediation_summary.pdf). As part of our SOC 2 evidence package we need: 1) a short verification letter from Redwood confirming which findings were retested and the validation approach used, and 2) an updated attestation/delta summary that we can include with our auditor.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can perform a focused retest on the high and critical items only, and provide a concise delta attestation (one page preferred) summarizing verification steps and outcomes? We would ideally have the validation completed and the attestation delivered by Feb 5 due to our audit schedule.

Also, please confirm whether you need any additional artifacts from our side besides the remediation summary — e.g., build IDs, patch tickets, or temporary test accounts.

Appreciate a quick note on scope and an estimated window.

Best,
Alice Jones
Head of InfoSec — Widgetly
alice.jones@widgetly.com

Attachment: widgetly_remediation_summary.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@widgetly.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-remediation validation request — Widgetly pen test (SOC2)

Thanks Alice — received and appreciate the clear ask.

Quick answers up front: we can scope a focused retest for high/critical findings and produce a short verification letter plus an updated attestation/delta summary. Feb 5 is tight but feasible if we lock a retest window early next week.

Two clarifying items so we scope correctly:
- Does Widgetly want active exploit attempts (exploit proof-of-concept) for every high finding, or are you comfortable with re-scan + targeted validation steps (reproduce, patch-check, config verification) for a subset and exploit verification for a smaller sample?
- For evidence, we typically need: remediation tickets (ticket IDs), a pre/post patch build or deployment tag if applicable, and a short note describing mitigation (config change, patch version, compensating control). If you can drop those into a shared Drive link we can avoid back-and-forth.

Proposed schedule: Redwood engineering run a re-scan Mon/Tue (Feb 1–2) and perform manual validation of 6 highest-risk items on Feb 3. Deliver a draft verification letter and delta report Feb 4, final by Feb 5. If that works for Widgetly we can proceed.

Vivek — looping you in to confirm the validation plan and sign off on the target item list. Marissa — can you prepare the delta report template and evidence checklist (one-pager)?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Jones <alice.jones@widgetly.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jan 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-remediation validation request — Widgetly pen test (SOC2)

On Fri, Jan 30, 2027 at 10:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed schedule: Redwood engineering run a re-scan Mon/Tue (Feb 1–2) and perform manual validation of 6 highest-risk items on Feb 3.

That plan looks good to me. A few specifics from the validation side:

1) Validation scope: we will target the 6 high/critical issues flagged in the RedTeam report. For each issue we will: (a) reproduce the original finding in a staging/test environment, (b) confirm remediation (patch installed or config changed), and (c) attempt a limited verification exploit when remediation type is config or access-related. We will not run a full adversary simulation as part of this retest unless Widgetly explicitly requests it.

2) Evidence deliverables: a one-page verification letter (signed by Redwood security), a concise delta report (bulleted items with pre/post status and evidence pointers), and a zip bundle with screenshots/scan outputs for the items we validate. Expected file names: remediation_delta_report_KP_v1.pdf, test-plan-scan-schedule.csv, and evidence_bundle.zip.

3) Considerations: If Widgetly requires proof-of-concept exploit code for any item we will coordinate scope and a safe execution plan; that will likely add 48–72 hours. Please state that explicitly if you need that.

We will proceed with the re-scan on Feb 1 unless we hear changes. Marissa — please assemble the delta report template and collect the target finding IDs.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Reliability & Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Attachment: remediation_delta_report_KP_v1.pdf (application/pdf); test-plan-scan-schedule.csv (text/csv)
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@widgetly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: securityops@widgetly.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-remediation validation request — Widgetly pen test (SOC2)

Thanks Kimberly and Vivek — that scope and the deliverables look perfect. We are comfortable with re-scan + limited exploit verification for a representative subset (exploit PoC only where necessary). No full adversary simulation required.

I have uploaded remediation tickets and build tags to the shared Drive link (see list below). Please proceed with the Feb 1–3 window. We also need the final verification letter and delta attestation as PDF attachments suitable for auditors.

Drive link: https://drive.widgetly.com/shared/SEC/audit-2027/remediation-evidence
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/abc123 (attestation signature requested)

If you can send the draft verification letter by Feb 4 we will route it to procurement and the auditor. Attached is our signed SLA exhibit for reference.

Best regards,
Alice Jones
